classification.difficultyReason: Two full annuity calculations per part, then a comparison. Part b mixes different rates and compounding frequencies. All the procedures are routine.

content.prompt: For each part, which investment is better? Compare the balances at the end of their respective investment terms. Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Leila can save $\$600$ at the end of each quarter for 10 years or $\$300$ at the end of each quarter for 20 years in a fund earning 4% p.a., compounded quarterly.

answer.short: $\$300$ quarterly for 20 years gives $\$36\,501.46$, compared with $\$29\,331.82$ for $\$600$ quarterly for 10 years: $\$7169.63$ more.
answer.worked:
Quarterly growth factor $r=1+\frac{0.04}{4}=1.01$.

Option 1: $\$600$ at the end of each quarter for 10 years, so $n=40$.
$$600(1.01)^{39}+600(1.01)^{38}+\cdots+600.$$
This is a geometric series with $a=600$, $r=1.01$ and $n=40$.
$$\begin{align*}FV_1&=\frac{600(1.01^{40}-1)}{0.01}\\FV_1&\approx\$29\,331.82\end{align*}$$
Option 2: $\$300$ at the end of each quarter for 20 years, so $n=80$.
$$\begin{align*}FV_2&=\frac{300(1.01^{80}-1)}{0.01}\\FV_2&\approx\$36\,501.46\end{align*}$$
Using the unrounded values:
$$FV_2-FV_1\approx\$7169.63$$
Therefore $\$300$ quarterly for 20 years gives the greater balance at its endpoint, by $\$7169.63$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Neil can invest $\$4800$ at the end of each year for 10 years in a fund earning 6% p.a., compounded annually, or $\$2400$ at the end of each six months for 10 years in a fund earning 5% p.a., compounded half-yearly.

answer.short: $\$4800$ yearly gives $\$63\,267.82$, compared with $\$61\,307.18$ for $\$2400$ half-yearly: $\$1960.64$ more.
answer.worked:
Option 1: $r=1.06$ and $n=10$ deposits of $\$4800$.
$$\begin{align*}FV_1&=\frac{4800(1.06^{10}-1)}{1.06-1}\\FV_1&\approx\$63\,267.82\end{align*}$$
Option 2: $r=1+\frac{0.05}{2}=1.025$ and $n=10\times2=20$ deposits of $\$2400$.
$$\begin{align*}FV_2&=\frac{2400(1.025^{20}-1)}{1.025-1}\\FV_2&\approx\$61\,307.18\end{align*}$$
Using the unrounded values:
$$FV_1-FV_2\approx\$1960.64$$
Therefore $\$4800$ yearly gives the greater balance, by $\$1960.64$.
